question: Can retained head06 regress source-specific identity through its frontal saddle/roof and simplified orbital opening despite pad reduction?

artifact.label: Frozen Advanced06, exact four matched pairs

decision_scope: Retain the technical checkpoint and selected sheet-treatment gains; reject blanket source-identity approval of head06. Reopen crown/brow/orbit macro organization before further head surfacing. No release or owner acceptance.
trigger: Parent reports material concordance of three initial roles. Their records were read as the conditional review's proposition to challenge, not counted as votes.

independence.model: Fresh context requested by parent as a different-model review; exact runtime model identity was not independently exposed or verified by this reviewer.
independence.source_limit: Same pinned development sources and frozen output images; no protected or external holdout.
independence.authority: Read local goal.md architect appendix and equilibrium SKILL.md; live GitHub goal verification is source-reported by initial reviewers, not repeated here.
independence.mutations: Only requested /tmp review JSON and /tmp image-check JSON written. No repository edits, children, installs, rendering, cloud transmission or publication.

hypothesis.statement: Head06 removes padded volume but weakens the source-specific hierarchy of swept crown, diagonal brow, recessed circular optic and bill-root break: a broad frontal cap and isolated circular annulus can make the head more generic than the matched before.
hypothesis.falsifier: Under the frozen matching cameras and both complete-bird lights, candidate must retain at least the before's clearly connected diagonal brow enclosure and non-isolated optic seat while replacing padding with source-like thin sheets. If the apparent cap/ring is limited to one highlight or close-up, disappears in profile/full-bird, or the source itself supports that same cap-plus-isolated-ring organization, this objection fails.
hypothesis.test_run: Directly inspected actual pinned locked full-bird and July head-only images, then all eight frozen before/candidate PNGs; verified the ten files against manifest sizes/hashes; compared render/camera control dictionaries excluding full_character_bounds; inspected head06 source only after image judgment.
hypothesis.result: Counterexample survives narrowly. The thinner sheets are a visible construction gain, but the head-neck pair exposes a more complete, visually isolated circular optic surround and shifts emphasis upward to a contiguous bright frontal roof. Profile and both full-bird lights retain that organization. Before's thick brow is padded and also wrong, but its continuous downward diagonal better encloses the optic. Neither version is a source match.
hypothesis.status: analytical interpretation supported by live pixel inspection
hypothesis.not_proven: No numerical likeness ranking, calibrated source-camera reconstruction, owner preference or proof that the entire after head is worse. Geometry-only causation was not isolated from surface/UV response.

decisive_evidence.observed: Both source heads integrate the circular optic into a substantial diagonal brow and curved cheek plate, with visible dark recess and a distinct armored bill root. Unequal swept rear leaves remain subordinate to this facial structure. Source includes broad armor: the objection is its organization and relationship to the eye, not a rule against broad plates.
decisive_evidence.scope: July head only; locked composite full bird. No July body/wing transfer.

decisive_evidence.observed: Before has inflated crown leaves and a thick continuous diagonal brow. After has thinner flatter pointed leaves and less padded jaw sheets, but the optic's upper/outer circular surround is more exposed and the forehead reads as broad adjoining roof courses. The cheek return still reads as a narrow strut beside a large empty opening; it is not the source's wider sculpted plate face.
decisive_evidence.inferred: Pad reduction does not by itself preserve the source's face hierarchy. The ring becomes a stronger graphic landmark and the threatening brow a weaker one.

decisive_evidence.observed: After's broad roof and distinct circular eye remain visible in profile and both complete-bird lighting conditions. Sharp leaf ends improve the rear head silhouette locally. Bill silhouette remains substantially the same and the head-to-body likeness gap remains large.
decisive_evidence.inferred: The counterexample is not explained solely by the close-up camera or workshop highlight. Full-bird improvement is too limited to treat head06 as a completed identity correction.

decisive_evidence.observed: Code hides the previous continuous swept diagonal brow and interleaved orbital cheek plates; creates five annular sheet sectors per side, segmented dorsal brow strips, and five frontal saddle sheets. Original optical assembly and upper bill are retained according to code.
decisive_evidence.inferred: This is a plausible construction cause for the changed visible hierarchy. The code alone does not establish the visible defect or shader causation.

claim_ledger.claim: Thinner pointed crown and nested jaw sheet treatment is retainable.
claim_ledger.consequence: Rejecting all head06 changes would discard a local construction gain.
claim_ledger.next_test: Keep sheet cross-sections and tips while changing their macro arrangement; compare new result against both before and06.

claim_ledger.claim: The complete head06 arrangement should be retained as an unqualified source-identity improvement.
claim_ledger.consequence: Further surfacing could entrench a generic cap-and-ring face.
claim_ledger.next_test: One bounded macro brow/orbit/saddle revision with unchanged camera, lights, pose and optics; fail if diagonal enclosure remains weaker than before.

claim_ledger.claim: The frozen comparison can distinguish the organization change from a camera/exposure change.
claim_ledger.consequence: A lighting or framing change could otherwise manufacture the effect.
claim_ledger.next_test: Continue these fixed controls; rendering reproduction and calibrated source-camera recovery remain separate.

next_macro_head_operator.retain: Thin sheet cross-sections, unequal pointed rear leaves, nested dark jaw-sheet treatment and preserved optic hardware; preserve stance/head frame.
next_macro_head_operator.change: Redistribute the frontal saddle into the source's visible brow-to-bill armor relationship. Form one legible diagonal supraorbital plate face that encloses the upper optic and connects to the bill-root step, with a distinct dark undercut. Integrate the circular seat into a wider curved cheek plate face around the opening; avoid leaving it as a freestanding round washer above a narrow strut. Break the smooth forehead-to-bill reading at the source's explicit panel seam. Sweep unequal crown leaves behind this facial structure rather than extending a broad top cap over it.
next_macro_head_operator.avoid: Do not restore padded tubes, shrink the optic arbitrarily, globally darken the scene, add fasteners as a substitute, or change source scope/stance.
next_macro_head_operator.acceptance_test: Re-render exact four pairs against06 and retained before. At full-bird scale under both lights, source-specific diagonal brow and recessed eye must become more legible while thin leaf/jaw gains persist. Confirm close-up and profile do not introduce a new cap, isolated ring or bill-root continuity defect. Stop or change approach if no visible gain.
